text:
Maya: heads up — opened a PR that consolidates the dedicated provisioning migration guide with a small autoscale SDK example and an isolation note. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2487 

Alex: skimming now. quick ask: can we make the SLA phrasing clearer about soft vs hard latency SLOs? current wording mixes percentiles. :eyes:

Sanjay: also, the terraform snippet in the migration section references `reserved_pool_id` but we don't show creating the reserved pool. can we add a one-liner example for creating a pool?

Maya: good catches. plan: 1) update SLA paragraph to separate soft/hard SLO bullets 2) add terraform create example (one-liner) and link to the reserved pools doc 3) fix autoscale snippet to use the new SDK API (we recently renamed set_scale_policy -> configure_autoscale)

Lucy: ran the current python snippet locally and got this warning: "DeprecationWarning: set_scale_policy will be removed in v0.12". So we should definitely switch to configure_autoscale. logs: ```
WARNING Deprecation: set_scale_policy used at docs/examples/autoscale.py:12
```

Patrick: for the autoscale example, prefer showing a target_utilization approach rather than min/max-only. Example idea (python):
```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient()
client.configure_autoscale(reserved_pool_id="rp-abc123", target_utilization=0.75, min_replicas=1, max_replicas=10)
```
This matches what the runtime expects and is easier to reason about for SLOs.

Alex: also, tiny link fix: the migration guide points to https://docs.redwood.dev/dedicated/old-provisioning which 404s. should be /dedicated/provisioning/migrate. doc-linter flagged it: `broken-link: line 78`.

doc-linter: broken-link detected in file docs/dedicated/migrate.md: line 78 -> https://docs.redwood.dev/dedicated/old-provisioning (404).

Maya: thanks — replaced that link and added a short paragraph calling out preemption behavior for best-effort workloads. I also added the terraform one-liner:```hcl
resource "redwood_reserved_pool" "example" {
  name = "migration-demo"
  gpu_count = 8
}
```

Sanjay: can we annotate the terraform snippet with a comment about isolation? e.g., `# use isolation_label to segregate shared tenants` — some customers assume pool creation implies tenant isolation by default.

Maya: added the isolation comment and a short blurb explaining that reserved pools are isolated by default but tenant-level eviction policies still apply.

Lucy: re-ran the updated snippet. python configure_autoscale call works, but one more nit: the example uses `target_utilization=0.75` without explaining units. added a parenthetical `(value is fraction of GPU util, e.g., 0.75 == 75%).`

Patrick: LGTM for the SDK snippet. Also suggest an inline example for the console UI mapping (how target_utilization maps to autoscale graphs) — one screenshot would be ideal but we can add a small ascii diagram for now.

Maya: added ASCII sparkline and a small mapping note. Also updated the SLA section to present: 1) soft SLOs (p50/p90 target guidance), 2) hard SLOs (p99 latency and auto-fallback policy), and 3) how isolation impacts observed latency.

Chris: reviewed the doc changes and left a couple inline nit comments about commas. approved on the content side. :thumbsup:

Alex: can we also add a short migration checklist bullet that tells customers to validate `eviction_protection` before migrating jobs? we've had a couple of customers hit preemption surprises.

Maya: added that checklist item and an example command to query pool metadata: `redwood-cli pools describe rp-abc123 --show-eviction-status`

doc-linter: link-check passed. spell-check: 2 suggestions (applied).

Maya: pushed all fixes to the PR (force-pushed updated branch) and requested reviews from @alex and @patrick. PR diff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2487/files

Alex: re-reviewed, looks clean. approving.

Patrick: approved. one minor followup task to add the console screenshot in a follow-up PR.

Chris: small punctuation nit fixed inline. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: PR merged into main by Maya (https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/commit/4f9a2d3). Release note: "docs(dedicated): consolidated migration + autoscale SDK examples; clarified SLA wording and isolation notes"

Maya: thanks team! I'll open the follow-up for the console screenshot and file a tiny chore to add an end-to-end validation script example.

Alex: thanks — great cleanup.

Sanjay: thanks, nice to have the terraform one-liner.

Lucy: nice quick turnaround. :rocket:
